what: ppm: Allowed signal deviation in m/z dimension
title: centWave Parameters
text: centWave parameter ppm specifies tolerance m/z values defining signal m/z dimension. parameter closely related mass accuracy mass spectrometer, traditionally expressed parts per million (ppm).  Higher ppm values allow greater variability m/z usually increase number detected features, may also increase number false positives. Lower values can lead missing signals, since measured mass values may deviate true mass expected (common). illustration shows peak picking example using LC-MS data, ppm parameter value varied centWave parameters held constant.

what: mzdiff: Accepted closeness of two signals in m/z dimension
title: centWave Parameters
text: mzdiff parameter specifies allowed minimum distance two co-eluting peaks m/z dimension. mzdiff value 1 indicates m/z value two signals overlapping scan time (=retention time) least 1 m/z, order signals included result peak list. centWave mzdiff parameter can also take negative values, indicating data point can allocated two different peaks. Assigning negative mzdiff values implications downstream processing steps, e.g., establishing correspondence overlapping peaks across different samples. example using data processed mzdiff values 1 0.01.

what: noise: Intensity cut-off, values below are not considered
title: centWave Parameters
text: many mass spectrometers, ion detection based electron-multiplier related detector technologies. instruments highly sensitive produce electronic noise, visible (usually) random data points certain intensity cut-. noise structure LC-MS spectra generated mass specs different types different vendors (incl. software updates) can inherently different, mz-value dependent noise intensities. Therefore, parameter requires careful adjustment mass spectrometer setup. Lower values increase centWave computation time, higher values lead missing true ion signals.

what: snthresh: Threshold of signal to noise ratio
title: centWave Parameters
text: Closely related noise structure snthresh parameter, allowing set minimal signal noise ratio (S/N) peaks detected. snthresh builds S/N estimate defines noise intensities locally scan time dimension:  local S/N definition can problematic noise homogeneous across m/z dimension. example shows higher intensity signals discarded higher snthresh values, likely nearby high-intensity noise points inflate local noise estimate around signal trace. final peak list using high snthresh parameter value contains signals low intensities, somewhat unexpected. UPDATE: BEHAVIOUR OBSERVED CENTWAVE FUNCTION PARAMETERISED SCANRANGE ARGUMENT (MSbrowser).

what: peakwidth: Range of peak elution times
title: centWave Parameters
text: peakwidth parameter specifies minimum maximum peak elution time seconds. optimal peakwidth parameter values related MS1 scan rate. Literature suggests minimum number six data points per peak order obtain reliable peak quantifications. Example: low intensity compound elutes 1s, number instrument scans least 6 per second. Increasing lower bound decreasing upper bound peakwidth makes peak detection restrictive can reduce number detected features, especially peaks unusually short long elution profiles. find optimal peakwidth parameter values, useful visually inspect elution times high low intensity ions different spectral regions. example shows results centWave peak picking performed different peakwidth parameter values parameters held constant. unexpected algorithm behaviour observed setting minimal elution time value 1, resulted peak splitting coherent signal split higher peakwidth values.

what: prefilter: Number of data points (k) exceeding a certain intensity threshold (I)
title: centWave Parameters
text: prefilter parameter similar noise parameter, instead specifying intensity cut-, specifies minimal number data points (k) exceed certain intensity value (). signal discarded represented less k consecutive data points intensity . Lower prefilter values less stringent allow low-intensity candidate signals pass initial filter, can increase computation time. Literature suggests minimum number six data points per peak order obtain reliable peak quantifications (also depending scan frequency) values parameter strongly depend characteristics well-behaved LC-MS signals. parameter set stringently can lead discarding true positive signals.

what: mzCenterFun: m/z summary statistic of a peak
title: centWave Parameters
text: final LC-MS feature table, feature characterised scan time m/z value. latter represents summary statistic data points defining feature, one slightly different m/z value (see also ppm parameter). mzCenterFun parameter specifies m/z summary statistic feature. practice, different mzCenterFun options little impact.

what: integrate: Integration method for peak quantification
title: centWave Parameters
text: integrate parameter specifies whether peak boundaries integration based original data (1) wavelet-transformed signal (2) (upper lower panel, respectively, plot ). former sensitive outliers noise, since centWave defines left right peak boundaries change slope (see Figure ). latter less sensitive noise, however, wavelet-filtered data less exact can lead signal mis-representations.

what: fitgauss: Peak parameterisation using Gaussian distribution
title: centWave Parameters
text: Gaussian function resembles characteristic symmetric “bell curve” shape, often described normal distribution. centWave parameter option set TRUE, Gaussian fitted feature. According xcms documentation, parametric fit mainly affects estimated retention-time position peak.

what: scanrange: Perform peak picking in a specific scan range
title: centWave Parameters
text: scanrange parameter allows define reduced scan/retention time interval peak picking performed entire m/z range. Spectral data outside scan time interval considered. Parameter scanrange specified scan indices rather seconds.

what: App installation and launch
title: Interactive LC-MS Data Exploration and Feature Analysis
text: MSbrowser hosted GitHub depends Bioconductor package xcms (version ≥ 3.6) feature detection. prompted, run package updates. MSbrowser can launched following R-terminal command: new web-browser window opens MSbrowser user interface.
code: # Install missing CRAN packages needed <- setdiff(c("devtools", "BiocManager"), installed.packages()[,"Package"]) if(length(needed)) install.packages(needed)  # Install or update xcms (>= 3.6) from Bioconductor if(!requireNamespace("xcms", quietly=TRUE) || packageVersion("xcms") < "3.6")   BiocManager::install("xcms")    # Install MSBrowser from GitHub devtools::install_github("tkimhofer/msbrowser") msbrowser::startApp()

what: Documentation
title: Interactive LC-MS Data Exploration and Feature Analysis
text: MSbrowser provides interactive workflow exploring raw LC-MS data tuning xcms peak picking parameters. Guidance available directly within user interface, additional resources provided : Practical guide centWave parameter tuning:centWave parameter guide MSbrowser supports open LC-MS data formats including mzML, mzXML, CDF, netCDF. Vendor-specific formats can converted using tools ProteoWizard GNPS.
